en: An observation deck with a beautiful night view. I think most girls like that kind of thing.
Oh, okay! Nice! And then he could pull ya in real close, and you could rest your cheek on his shoulder...
Well, I didn't say all that.
Hehe, whoops! I guess I let my imagination run away there.
No matter. I think you've given our readers a very good suggestion.
Now for the last question of the interview. If you were over eighteen, do ya think you would ever consider having sex with a middle-aged man?
Hey, it is the last question and all, so I thought, what the heck? It'd be a great way to end the article, too.
So, what do ya think? Would you have sex with a middle-aged man?
Okay, okay. I know that was an indelicate question, but you gotta gimme something to work with here!
Aww, c'mon! Whaddya expect me to do, make up an article outta thin air?
What, did I make ya mad or somethin'? I'm sorry, but this is the nature of my job. You gotta gimme a break, here.
No, I wouldn't.
Aww. No dice, huh?
Well, I had to ask.
Kind of a disappointin' ending for our readers, though.
Not gonna answer that one, huh? Well, at least our readers can interpret that to mean whatever they want. Hehe.
I'm not really sure, but I think, maybe, if I was in love with him.
Seriously!? Wow! Boy, am I glad I asked!
Hehehe. This'll be great. Thanks a bunch for that juicy nugget!
Well, that just about wraps it up. Thanks for bein' so patient, and I'm sorry for askin' ya such inappropriate questions.
That's all right. I understand you were just doing your job.
I can see why you're so popular. You've got a new fan in me. I'm rootin' for ya!
Thanks for your time. I hope we can do another interview soon.
Well, that just about wraps it up. I know you're an idol, so there's only so much you can say. I guess ya did a pretty decent job.
Although, I did kinda hope you'd give me a little more, ya know, provocative answers.
Well, I wish you good luck. I hope we can do this again sometime.
Of course. Thank you for coming today.
So that's the end of the interview, I guess. That was abysmal. A complete waste of my time.
Look, as an idol, you're gonna have to do tons of interviews. If ya can't handle little things like this, you'd be better off givin' up now.
"Gossip Gals" is a fairly hard-hitting gossip magazine.
I didn't know this until after I'd accepted the interview, but the editorial department of "Gossip Gals" is in good with Osaka Talent.
They might try to talk T-Set up and put you down, so watch out for that kind of thing.
The interviewer will be Masuda-san. He refers to himself as "creepy, but in a cute way."
The interview will be about your relationships with friends, and any feuds you have going with rivals.
Be very careful not to bad-mouth anybody. They'll twist your words and your image will be tarnished.
(The interview is going to be about my friends and rivals.)
(But I have to be sure not to bad-mouth anyone.)
Whew! I finally made it. I'm here for the interview.
(Oh! Is that the interviewer?)
Hello. I'm Masuda, from "Gossip Gals." You ready for this?
I think so. Thank you very much for coming.
Hmm. You're much more reserved than I expected. After seeing you on TV, I thought you'd have more of a... charismatic aura.
Anyway, let's get on with it, shall we? Have you already been told what today's interview is going to be about?
So... you weren't told anything? Well, that is a problem.
As I've already explained to your manager, I am here to talk to you about your relationships with friends and any feuds you have going on with other idols.
Well, never mind. The truth is, what I really want to hear about is all the dirt you have on your rivals. Come on, give me something juicy to write about!
I'm very sorry to disappoint you, but that's not the sort of thing I do.
Aww, come on. Let your guard down a little, won't you?
I was told it would be about my relationships with friends.
Yep, that's it! And⑬more importantly⑬I want to know about your rivals!
Our readers really love the juicy stuff. You know, backstabbing, bad-mouthing. The nastier the better, I always say!
Well, I'm very sorry to disappoint you, but I don't have anything like that for you.
Let's see. Was it about being harassed by T-Set?
Yikes. Is that what you were told? I'm sure I didn't say anything like that.
But if that's what you want to talk about, by all means. Actually, that would be pretty great!
Let's see. Was it about who I consider to be a rival?
Eh? Well, not exactly.
I told your manager I wanted to talk to you about your relationships with friends and any feuds you have with other idols.
Well, on to the good stuff. First off, let me ask you about the Princess League. You've been pretty much crushing the competition, haven't you?
Even to the untrained eye like mine, it's easy to see you're head and shoulders above the rest.
Given your superior talent, what do you think of all those girls who just aren't on your level?
Hmm. So you're saying their level of talent is so low, it's not even worth your time to talk about?
What? I didn't say that at all.
Well, if you don't say anything, that's the way I'm going to take it. Makes for a good article that way.
I don't think I'm better than any of the girls participating in the Princess League. They're all good competition.
But you've been winning against every single one of them, right? Doesn't that mean you're too good for them?
We're all giving it everything we have in this competition. Each performance is won or lost by very slim margins.
Hmm. What a carefully worded answer. You know, I think your manager warned you not to say what you really think.
It kind of defeats the point, actually. I hope you'll be a little more forthcoming the rest of the interview.
I won't say who, but I think some of them aren't taking this work seriously. They haven't practiced nearly enough, in my opinion.
Oho! That's the stuff I like to hear! Nobody's going to make it in this idol industry without putting in the hard hours, right?
That's exactly right.
Yeah! Enough with these girls who think they can scrape by on a little bit of cuteness and no effort. What a great quote, Haruka-chan!
Wait, but...
That's a loaded question, don't you think?
I mean, it's true, isn't it? That's why you've been able to get this far. Because the other girls just aren't talented enough.
Oh, that sounds like a rather malicious way of thinking to me.
<Italic>Well</Italic>, you're welcome to take it that way if you want, but don't you think you ought to watch the way you talk to an adult?
Now, let's talk about T-Set, of Osaka Talent. You do know who they are, don't you?
Yes. I do.
They used to belong to Dyna Chair, you know. But then they decided to jump ship for Osaka Talent. Must leave a bad taste in your mouth, wouldn't you say?
So in light of all that, what do you think about T-Set being called the number one idols in Osaka right now?
No comment, huh? Or do you just refuse to acknowledge T-Set's success?
Oh no, that's not what I meant at all.
But if you don't answer, I'll have to write something like, "When I asked Haruka this, her face clouded over and she fell silent."
It doesn't really bother me. After all, it's not like we both belonged to Dyna Chair at the same time.
And I'm sure my agency was of the mindset that they were free to go as they pleased.
You're kidding me, right? Dyna Chair must've sunk a lot of money into getting them ready for their debut. That has to sting.
If I were the president of Dyna Chair, I'd be hoping for their downfall right about now.
Well, that's not the way we think.
Hmm. If you say so. But it doesn't make for a very interesting interview.
I don't think that'll be true for long. I believe you have to follow a certain code of ethics in order to maintain the trust of your fans.
Fair point! But, Dyna Chair never did manage to make T-Set as popular as they've gotten with Osaka Talent.
Now, Haruka-chan, I don't think even you can deny that Osaka Talent has done a fine job of selling T-Set. It isn't at all surprising that Dyna Chair would be bitter about that.
But, I guess it's really T-Set that's to blame. Their success is bound to earn resentment from those below them. Whew, the idol business sure is rough!
I have no objection to it whatsoever. I consider them great competition, and what happened between them and my agency doesn't involve me.
Well! I can see they coached you well. I was hoping you'd give me a little bit more to work with.
I'm just saying what I feel. We're friendly rivals, and that's it.
Hmm. I guess you're being cautious. To be honest, I thought I'd be able to get some juicer quotes out of you.
Okay, last question. I was told by T-Set's manager that Dyna Chair and T-Set got into a little tussle. Is that true?
Oh, you don't know? A manager of yours named Horie grabbed one of the T-Set girls' arms and screamed at her. You were apparently right there when it happened.
With rumors like this flying around, people are starting to say Dyna Chair is using you as a weapon of vengeance against Osaka Talent. Were you aware of this growing sentiment?
You know, you haven't made a single comment this whole interview. Well, better for me. Your silence has given me plenty to write about.
Heheh. I'm gonna make a juicy article out of this! I don't suppose Dyna Chair will like it much, though.
You don't deny it? Haha! This is beautiful! Shocked speechless, are you?
I'm not aware of being used as a weapon because it's not true. That much I do know.
Hmm. So you're saying Horie-san didn't scream at one of the T-Set girls?
Of course he didn't. Just before that, she had tripped me. Horie-san was defending me by confronting them about the incident. He wasn't screaming at her.
But he was certainly raising his voice in anger, wasn't he? Some would call that screaming.
Plus, I heard that your claim of being "tripped" was really just a misunderstanding.
Hehe. I think maybe Dyna Chair has a bit of a persecution complex.
But thanks for confirming the story on Horie-san. That should really spice up my article!
Dyna Chair isn't seeking revenge. We have a healthy rivalry, and it's purely friendly.
Oh? So you're saying that Horie-san <Italic>didn't</Italic> get into an argument with T-Set?
He did, but it had nothing to do with revenge. It was just a minor workplace disagreement, not something worth publicizing.
Ugh. You're not giving me much to write about, you know.
I'm just answering your question truthfully.
Hmph. You're a lot tougher than they said.
That's ridiculous. Dyna Chair isn't using me, as a weapon or otherwise. And I really don't have anything else to say about it.
Hmm. Are you sure you want to take that tone with me? It might affect what I write, you know.
I believe you're the one who is setting the tone. I don't know how else to answer.
Hmph. You're a lot tougher than you look. One might even say you're downright stubborn at times.
Well, I don't think I'll use that question after all. I'm sorry if I was rude.
Okay, that's the end of the interview. To be honest, I didn't get close to what I was after.
What you were after?
I was looking for something to tarnish your image with, of course. You know the saying. "The nail that sticks out gets hammered down."
I won't say who, but certain people wanted to see you brought down a peg or two. They asked me to write an article with that in mind.
But you stood firm, and didn't give me a single opening. It looks like you win, kid.
I hope you'll give me a chance to interview you again. Without any funny business this time.
Anyhow, I think you just gained yourself a brand-new fan! Heheh. I'll be going now.
Okay, that's the end of the interview. To be honest, I was hoping to get a bit more out of you.
You see, I was told to find something to tarnish your image with.
But you barely gave me an opening. Not a perfect job, but you came pretty close.
Oh. I see.
I'm sorry. I wish the circumstances could've been different. But we're such a small magazine, we have to do what the powers that be want.
Well, I'll be going now. Thank you for your time today.
Well, that's the end of the interview. Heheh. I'd say I did pretty good.
Sorry to say, but I was told to find something to tarnish your image with.
